summary: All 36 automated checks pass. The only CR-004 edits in sim.js are the two figures: dummy.maxHealth and impact.maxPay are both 1600, and nothing else changed. The hand-computed damage values match the build's grid exactly. The code review found no blocking defect. The level 3 stall-breaker figures, the human-only playtest items and a few acceptance criteria that no check covers directly are reported below as unverified or as notes.

criteria.evidence: Checks load_sim, sim_is_pure and modules_exist_and_do_the_work pass. api exports PARAMS, Damage, Vehicles, createSim and step, and window.DummiesSim is set. Reading sim.js, there is no DOM, timer, Date or Math.random.
params_match_spec reports 256 parameters identical. createSim does clone(PARAMS). The impact object has none of the removed keys.
walk_frame_rate_independent: 203.2 px at 60 Hz vs 202.8 px at 120 Hz. run_speed_matches_spec passes. Class speeds in PARAMS are 138/120/192/108/144/156.
deterministic_and_seeded passes. The sim uses only the mulberry-style rnd(), and the write-off timing uses no draws.
attract_then_confirm passes. createSim sets mode play when autostart is set. spawnStep returns at once when traffic is false.
lunge_distance_equal_8_directions: 164.0 px in all eight directions. lunge_frame_rate_independent: 164.0 px at 120 Hz.
held_lunge_does_not_chain: 1 lunge in 3 s. Fresh-press logic: fl = lunge && !prevLunge.
lunge_distance check includes the facing direction. dummyStep uses d.facing when no direction is held.
lunge_eases_out: 87% at half time. ease3 is applied per step as a difference of p(t), so the 0.875 target holds.
recovery_is_tweened: recovery 0.35 s, moved 19.6 px. dummyStep applies the easeOutQuad factor f.
dummyStep clamps to the hall after the lunge or walk step. pushOut clamps again.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right passes. Level geometry and spawn entries in PARAMS and drawEntry are lane-based. The top-left corner is clear because the entry minimum is 200.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right (14 cars in 60 s, never stalls). levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic: L1 ends at 61 to 64 s.
level2_cross_no_collisions: 18 horizontal and 24 vertical cars, no overlap. drawEntry for the cross level picks only edge 0 or edge 2.
level2_cross_no_collisions, level3_free_for_all and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play report no overlap. axisMove truncates against every car.
Give-way is in carsStep: it yields only to b.serial < c.serial, skips a b that is behind, and sets held and braking. The Vehicles audit shows a following car stops with gap >= 7.8 px.
level3_free_for_all: 4 directions, 6 classes. drawEntry draws the edge and a lateral value in [200,520] or [200,800].
PARAMS levels 14/2/3, 20/3/6 and 28/5/12. spawnStep checks vehiclesSpawned < allocation and draws units from the first L.pool entries.
write_off_animation_then_card passes. writeOff() sets mode writeoff and state.writeOff on the hit step and leaves card and ending null. dismiss() restores health to maxHealth.
level_progression, ending_decommissioned and levelEnd order (noncompliant, then decommissioned, then card). Confirm in over calls resetRun, which sets mode attract.
ending_licensed passes. writeOffEnd calls finish('licensed') after the animation. The target of 11 sits between the quota sum of 10 and the allocation total of 62.
tail_contact_pays_its_small_share (van tail 7). The damage grid shows sedan tail 5 and 25. d.lungeReach is exactly 1 at full health.
html_static passes. index.html has no http:// or https://, loads sim.js with a script tag, and steps at STEP = 1/60 with an accumulator. Font stacks keep the Testpad names first.
Needs a person to look at the drawing. The code draws roads, shoulders, barriers, level name and number, HUD, cards, attract screen and perception. Math.random is used only for shake and particles.
Playtest. Level end times of 61 to 92 s were measured with a dummy standing on the road.
damage_module_is_logical and damage_in_play_matches_module. Damage.assess implements min(maxPay, round(base*share*lf*mf)) and ignores dummy velocity.
The damage grid matches the calibration. Sedan nose lunge is 500 against a maximum of 1600, so no single hit writes off a fresh body.
dummy_cannot_walk_through_a_car and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play. pushOut ends with a clamp and a nearestClear fallback.
carsStep never reads dummy solidity. The dummy is excluded from axisMove, and pushOut moves only the dummy.
solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play and vehicle_numbers_for_qa. Barrier clearance minimums are 9 px on level 1 and 3 px on level 2. limits() and latMove clamp lateral position.
No check walks the dummy from y=100 to y=500. Reading dummyStep, no barrier logic touches the dummy.

Not directly named in the check list. detection_commit_and_brake_flags (VAN-07 seen, lock 1) and swFeasible show side selection within the barrier limits. The shoulder-use count across a seeded batch was not reported.
No named check. The code path exists: if neither side is feasible, stuck=true leaves the car unlocked, and it brakes through the (brakeFirst || stuck) branch.
level3_free_for_all and solid_cars checks report no overlap. latFree includes the oncoming-band test. spawnStep waits on oncoming bands on level 3.

No check places the dummy idle at (60,60). traffic_audit reports a longest stop of 0 s on L1 and L2. On L3 with a wandering dummy the longest stop is 22 s, and that level is not enforced by the check.
Playtest. The code draws barriers with gaps at the junction (drawBarriers) and returns early on level 3.
Playtest.
level2_cross_no_collisions. Arrows are drawn for both roads in drawRoads.

No check measures the lowest-serial hold with the stallLimit+1 criterion. The breaker report shows a longest hold of 6 s with an idle dummy and 21.8 s with a wandering dummy on L3. The figure does not say whether the dummy was in the detection zone.
levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play pass. Every run ended, in 61 to 92 s. Levels 1 and 2 had 0 breaker removals.

No scripted breaker test is listed. stallStep removes only cars with a higher serial near L, once stallT >= 6 s, and does not touch vehiclesSpawned or score. L3 removals (5 in the audit) show it works.

Code review. Damage has exactly contactFace and assess and reads only its arguments. 2300, perMomentum, lungeBonus and the faceNose-family names do not appear in sim.js. The only outside arithmetic is sev = pay / maxPay, which is severity.

Damage.contactFace follows the spec zone rules. Only the sedan-grid output was verified by running, so the boundary table was checked by reading. The strict comparisons match the table, e.g. (31,0) is flank and (31.01,17.01) is frontCorner.
damage_grid matches the formula for all six classes (see damage_audit). The sedan momentumFactor is 1.
By reading assess: the shares are monotone, the lunge multiplier is exactly 5, a non-lunging dummy gets lf 1, and speed 0 gives mf 0 and damage 0. damage_module_is_logical passes.
damage_in_play_matches_module (diagonal flank lunge x0.3, x5). Direction does not enter assess.
damage_in_play_matches_module. judge() records the full lastImpact fields and applies the same res.damage to score and health. lastImpact is null from resetRun.
hit_during_any_lunge_step_counts_as_a_lunge. judge uses snap positions and outsidePoint, the zone is judged by contactFace before pushOut, and d.lungedThisStep covers the final step.
judge consumes the hit, sets levelContact and lastImpact, and returns without changing health or score when pay <= 0. The momentum factor uses c.speed.
modules_exist_and_do_the_work and vehicle_numbers_for_qa. The speed audit shows max increase 6 px per step (the limit) and 13 over-limit decreases, all attributed to truncation, none to other causes.
Rest to cruise matches the expected time per class, e.g. sedan 0.383 s measured vs 0.383 s expected. Stopping gap is 7.8 to 7.9 px, no touch.
Lane deviation is 0 on all three levels. traffic_audit: 0 cars removed inside the hall on L1 and L2.

Code review. Car fields are written only in placeCar, spawnStep, carsStep, latMove, axisMove and stallStep, all in the Vehicles section. The cars array is written elsewhere only in startLevel (reset). The only dummy.health reduction in step is in judge, and it uses res.damage.

This report contains the damage table, the Lawrence cases, the vehicle numbers, barrier clearances, write-off numbers and the stall-breaker counts (3/30 idle, 9/30 wandering). The body-health arithmetic and write-off numbers come from code reading. A step count at 1/60 and 1/120 was not run by the checks. All damage values match within 0.
Playtest. The numbers are logically consistent.
PARAMS.writeOff.duration = 1.1.

write_off_animation_then_card. writeOff() counts the body, adds the bonus, clears lunging, recovering and velocity, and sets state.writeOff { t:0, duration, x, y }. The same function covers the licensed-winning hit.

write_off_animation_then_card (frozen, confirm ignored). The writeoff branch of step only adds dt to time and writeOff.t and updates prevLunge and prevConfirm. Vehicles.step and the dummy step are not called, so there are no draws.
Animation measured at 1.10 s. The exit test is w.t >= duration, followed by writeOffEnd (card kind writeoff or finish licensed). The 1/120 step count was not measured.
Confirm in the card branch is fresh-press only (fc). prevConfirm is updated every step, including during writeoff, so a held key is not fresh.
Playtest. Drawing code present: shake 14*(1-u)^2, red blend over u/0.25, smoothstep fade to gone from u 0.85, 18 particles.
index.html reads S.writeOff.t / duration in drawDummy and frame. It adds no fields to state. sim.js has no particle or shake code.
Playtest.
PARAMS.dummy.maxHealth and PARAMS.impact.maxPay are both 1600, and resetDummy sets health from params. front_impact_pays_once shows health 1600.0 at start. The string 2300 does not appear in sim.js.

By arithmetic from the grid: 500 per lunge gives 1100, 600, 100, then a write-off with health floored at 0 (damage recorded 500, health lost 100). 16 x 100 = 1600 gives a write-off on the 16th walking hit. Severity 500/1600 = 0.3125. No check ran this sequence.

By reading dummyStep: repair is (maxHealth / fullTime) * dt, giving 53.3 points per second and 30 s to full. Reach is 1 - 0.55*(1 - h/1600), 0.725 at h=800 and exactly 1 at 1600. No check ran this. PARAMS differ from the previous release only in the two body-health fields.
Playtest. The arithmetic is 3,200 points for 2 bodies, about 8 lunges with overkill, in an allocation of 14 cars.

defects.problem: Level 3 stall breaker removes cars in about 3 of 30 idle runs and 9 of 30 wandering runs (5 cars removed inside the hall in the traffic audit). The longest hold of the lowest-serial car was 21.8 s, and the longest stop of any car was 22 s. The breaker is a spec-mandated safety net and QA only reports it, but it fires more often than 'not in normal play'.
Cosmetic: an extra pointer-down lunge input could press lunge while a card is dismissed. This is harmless because confirm and lunge are separate fresh-press edges.

damage_audit.comment: Every value is round(100 x share x lunge x mf), with mf = 1 for the sedan and 108x3/138 = 2.3478 for the bus. Shares fall from nose to tail. The lunge value equals 5 times the walking value before rounding, and the build is within 1 of it. Direction and dummy speed are ignored by assess. Speed 0 pays 0. The largest value, 1174, is below the 1600 cap. In sim.js the only code that changes health or score on impact is judge(), and it uses Damage.assess output. The remaining score change is the write-off bonus in writeOff().

vehicle_audit.paths: Cars keep their lane exactly with no dummy (deviation 0 on all levels). Lateral motion happens only through swerve, flip or return-to-lane, and is clamped to the barrier limits (limits()) and gated by latFree (free space and, on level 3, oncoming-band checks). Measured barrier clearance with a wandering dummy is 9 px on level 1 and 3 px on level 2. Direction never changes. On level 3 cars stay at their spawn lateral coordinate.
vehicle_audit.stop_start: Reasons to slow: the dummy in the detect zone (brake factor, brakeFirst or stuck), the caution derate, give-way to a lower-serial car by sweep intersection, truncation against another car, and swerve infeasibility. Cars restart at accel (360 px/s^2) once the sweep is clear, with rest-to-cruise times matching expected (sedan 0.383 s). Cruise-to-stop measured 3.7 to 4.05 s against an expected 0.18 to 0.32 s. The note explains that the car starts slowing at its look-ahead distance and then closes the gap slowly, ending 7.8 to 7.9 px short of the stopped car, with no touch. Max decrease per step was 156 px, from 13 truncation steps, none from other causes. On levels 1 and 2 the longest stop was 0 s. On level 3 the longest stop was 22 s, and 13 cars stopped.
vehicle_audit.removal: Cars leave in two ways: wholly outside the hall, past the edge they travel toward (carsStep filter), or the stall breaker (stallStep). The breaker deletes without score. It removed 0 cars on L1 and L2, and 5 cars on L3 in the 3 runs of the traffic audit (3 of 30 idle runs and 9 of 30 wandering runs in the 30-seed audit). Nothing else deletes cars, and startLevel's empty array is a level reset.
concerns: Level 3 relies on the stall breaker to clear jams in roughly 10 to 30% of 60 s runs. This is within the spec and was reported, not fixed.
The lowest-serial car's longest hold was 21.8 s with a wandering dummy. It is unclear how much of that was the dummy standing in its detection zone, which resets the breaker timer.

notes: CR-004 is implemented as specified. The change is exactly the two figures in sim.js PARAMS (dummy.maxHealth 1600, impact.maxPay 1600), and index.html has no 2300.

The write-off animation is confirmed in code: the writeoff branch is a freeze that only advances the timers and updates prevLunge and prevConfirm, so confirm is ignored. It lasts 1.1 s, then goes to the card or the Licensed ending. index.html draws the decaying shake, red blend, fade to gone by u 0.85 and an 18-particle burst. Whether it looks right is unverified.
Spawn-unit choice differs from the Testpad (uniform among free pool units, per spec). Report signatures now count tail and rear-corner contacts as paid hits, which the spec allows.
Several criteria (AC-31 to AC-33, AC-35, AC-39, AC-41) have no directly named check. The code paths exist and the related checks pass, but QA could only read them.
Dummy at health 800 repairs at 53.3 points per second after 1.5 s, derived from reading the code and not run.
